findings.title: Secret-bearing temp file is briefly left at umask permissions (0644) before chmod to 0600
findings.source: Rotated OAuth tokens (refresh_token/access_token/id_token) serialized by FileCredentialReader.writeBack (Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Credentials/FileCredentialReader.swift:74), and other 0o600 callers (config.toml with inline api_key)
findings.sink: Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Cache/AtomicFileWrite.swift:19 creates the temp file with the default mode (0666 & ~umask, so 0644). The 0o600 chmod only happens afterwards, at line 21-24.
findings.description: The temp file is fully created and populated with the secret payload by `Data.write(.atomic)`, which gives new files the default mode. `setAttributes(0o600)` runs only after that. For that interval the plaintext tokens sit world-readable in the destination directory. The doc comment claims this race is avoided, but it has only moved from the final path to the temp path. That breaks the hard rule of '0o600 at write time'. For ~/.codex, which the app does not force to 0700 (only its own Application Support and Caches dirs get 0700), the directory is typically traversable by other local users.
findings.exploit_scenario: On a multi-user Mac, another local user watches ~/.codex with kqueue/FSEvents for `.auth.json.*.tmp` and calls open() the moment the file appears. An fd opened while the mode is 0644 keeps its read access after the chmod and rename. The attacker then reads the rotated Codex refresh_token and can take over the victim's ChatGPT/Codex session.
preconditions: another local OS user on the same Mac
~/.codex (or the destination dir) is traversable by others (not 0700)
manage_oauth_refresh = true for the Codex write-back path (off by default); config.toml writes land in the 0700 app-support dir, so they are not reachable
findings.impact: Disclosure of a rotated OAuth refresh token (Codex) to another local user
findings.fix: Create the temp file with the final mode from the start: open(tmp, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600) (or mkstemp + fchmod before any write), write, fsync, then rename(2). Do not use Data.write(.atomic) for this.
findings.evidence: AtomicFileWrite.swift:19 `try data.write(to: tmp, options: .atomic)` then :20-24 `if let permissions { try FileManager.default.setAttributes([.posixPermissions: ...], ofItemAtPath: tmp.path) }`. FileCredentialReader.swift:74 passes permissions: 0o600 for ~/.codex/auth.json. Paths.swift:86-102 ensureDir does not tighten the mode of ~/.codex.
